item.title: Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026?
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi It appears music powerhouse Ayodeji Balogun is keeping his fans hanging too long on a thread after he made a promise of his seventh solo studio album “coming soon” in June 2026. Three months down the line, the wait continues without any actual date in sight. The Wizkid FC, his fanatical fans, wouldn’t throw any tantrum about this, but the question has to be asked as to what is keeping the “Holla at Ya Boy” star from unleashing his “Sexy” (title of his seventh studio album) on the music scene. The fact that the superstar started 2026 on the up and up hasn’t helped matters because it felt pretty much like he gave his fans a shot in the arm and left them high and dry. He began the year with ‘Jogodo’, a collaboration with Asake that set the stage for their joint extended play, ‘REAL, Vol. 1’. He subsequently expanded his catalogue with releases involving Latin music, British R&B and other contemporary sounds, reinforcing his reputation as an artiste comfortable working across musical boundaries. One of the defining moments of his 2026 output was the January release of ‘REAL, Vol. 1’, a four-track EP with Asake. Released on January 23, the project brought together two generations of Nigerian music stars whose styles have helped shape the contemporary Afrobeats sound. The project followed the success of their earlier collaborations, including ‘MMS’ on Asake’s 2024 album, ‘Lungu Boy’. It featured songs such as ‘Jogodo’, ‘Iskolodo’ and ‘Turbulence’, combining infectious rhythms, melodic hooks and elements of contemporary African dance music. ‘Jogodo’, released ahead of the EP in January, served as the lead single and generated anticipation for the full project. The collaboration offered fans an opportunity to hear the two singers build on their established musical chemistry. The singer continued this international run with ‘Alive’, a collaboration with British singer-songwriter Jorja Smith, released on July 2. The song blended R&B and Afrobeats, with production by P2J, and appeared ahead of Smith’s third studio album, ‘What Are The Odds’. Another notable release was ‘Coca Body’, featuring Dutch rapper and singer Frenna, British-Nigerian singer Odeal and Wizkid. Released in July, the song brought together the artistes’ melodic approaches in a record that drew on Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop influences. These collaborations highlighted Wizkid’s continued willingness to explore different sounds while maintaining the relaxed vocal delivery that has become a hallmark of his music. Beyond his recorded collaborative outputs, his fans still await his next solo effort. In June, he unveiled ‘Sexy’ as the title of his seventh studio album at a listening party in Paris. However, a release date and full tracklist had not been announced at the time of the report. The post Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026? appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions
item.description: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disbursed the sum of ₦38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions, nationwide, under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund. Details of the disbursement contained in a statement by the Head, Media Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie in Abuja, yesterday, showed that beneficiaries included 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education. The funds would support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions. The university component accounts for ₦28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling ₦5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education received ₦4.7 billion. The statement read in part, “The intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). “The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria. The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity.” The post FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions appeared first on Vanguard News .

Soludo said he had since, communicated APGA’s position to President Tinubu during the President’s visit to Anambra to inaugurate landmark projects, including the Government House, Solution Fun City and roads. Defends Tinubu’s economic reforms On the removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, Aburime said Soludo supported Tinubu’s economic policies, describing them as painful but necessary measures to address longstanding structural weaknesses. He argued that the previous practice of printing money to sustain the economy was unsustainable, adding that the reforms would eventually yield benefits. On whether Tinubu had influenced former President Muhammadu Buhari to adopt better economic policies, Aburime said it was impossible to know whether the President had offered such advice behind the scenes, noting that influence did not guarantee acceptance. Kanu’s release will be resolved politically On the continued detention of Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, Aburime said the matter had assumed a political dimension and would ultimately require a political resolution. Asked why the governor had yet to achieve that objective despite his closeness and relationship with Tinubu, Aburime declined to comment extensively but said efforts towards a resolution were not over. “The Nnamdi Kanu case has become a political case and it will be resolved politically,” he said. Monday sit-at-home defeated, Anambra back to life Soludo declared that the enforcement of the Monday sit-at-home order by armed groups had been defeated, with commercial and social activities returning to normal across Anambra. item.title: Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss
item.description: Michael Carrick said he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future as manager into doubt on Sunday. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford. “It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know. “I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along, I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.” Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported Carrick as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players. “I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick. “I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.” Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired. Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after a 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday. “There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.” The post Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man United’s misery continues, suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth
item.description: Manchester United slumped further into crisis with a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday that plunged Michael Carrick’s future as manager into doubt. Carrick’s bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United’s winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won 3-0 at Old Trafford as goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved win for Marco Rose’s side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season’s Premier League player of the year was a “purely football” driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” from the Bournemouth fans. But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago. A strong finish to last season during Carrick’s interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League, but was aided by a lack of European or domestic cup football. United have won just twice — against newly-promoted Ipswich and Azerbaijani side Sabah — in 12 games in all competitions this season. Bournemouth began the day behind the Red Devils in the table after a difficult start for Rose. But just three days after beating AC Milan 3-0, they outclassed another giant of the European game. Rayan opened the floodgates when he connected sweetly with Justin Kluivert’s free-kick on 38 minutes. Five minutes later, Leny Yoro stumbled under pressure from Adrien Truffert and the French full-back had a simple task to square for Tavernier to tap into an empty net. Many expected Fernandes to be stripped and ready for the start of the second half, but he remained on the bench and the United performance got no better. Inside the first minute of the restart Evanilson found the net, but was flagged offside. That let-off mattered little as Bournemouth could have run out even more convincing winners. Senne Lammens denied Rayan before the Brazilian winger fired wide after racing past Lisandro Martinez. Evanilson did finally add a third 20 minutes from time when he rounded Lammens before curling in an exquisite finish from a narrow angle. The United support unleashed their fury at the club’s unpopular owners, the Glazer family, rather than Carrick in the closing stages. Carrick applauded the Stretford End and touched his chest as he made his way down the tunnel. However, it is the manager who will likely be the fall guy after another miserable afternoon for the 20-time English champions. The agency said hospitals should maintain effective screening and triage systems, promptly separate suspected cases from other patients, notify public health authorities and apply appropriate infection prevention and control precautions. These measures include hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, injection safety, safe handling of sharps, proper waste management and the appropriate use of personal protective equipment. The NCDC’s warning is directed at preventing delays that could expose other patients, healthcare workers and caregivers before a suspected infection is recognised and the necessary precautions are implemented. item.title: 2027: Bishop rallies northern christians for Tinubu
item.description: Bishop John Praise Daniel, has urged Christians across northern Nigeria to unite across denominational, ethnic and political differences to support 2027 re-election bid of President Bola Tinubu. Daniel, who is the General Overseer of Dominion Chapel International made the call at the commissioning of the national secretariat of Arewa Christians for Tinubu (ACT)2027 in Abuja. He said unity was essential to achieving the organisation’s political objectives, urging Northern Christians to prioritise their interests and vision over religious denominational differences and tribal affiliations. He said a collective agreement and cooperation would strengthen the group’s capacity to achieve its objectives. “When we are united, there is no impossibility that will stand against us,” he said. The bishop expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.” Daniel urged ACT-2027 members to take their mobilisation efforts to communities across the region, including villages, local government areas and wards, to sensitise Christians about the group’s political agenda. He advised against allowing tribal affiliations and political differences to undermine the movement, insisting that members should work together irrespective of their diverse backgrounds. “We cannot be divided on politics and tribes. When we see something that is good, we hold to it and stand together,” he said. item.title: Inter rally late to down Fiorentina and regain Serie A lead
item.description: Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina at San Siro on Sunday and return to the summit of Serie A. Alex Jimenez’s rocket strike had the struggling visitors heading for a shock win, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute. The result meant the Nerazzurri returned to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club’s winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot. Cristian Chivu’s side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, who made a fingertip stop on a Pio Esposito header before showing quick reactions to parry Thuram’s angled drive. De Gea was alert again to parry a fierce Thuram strike over the bar early in the second half, but it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes. Former AC Milan player Alex Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner. Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser, with Carlos Augusto’s glancing header coming off the top of the bar and De Gea denying substitute Petar Sucic, but they could not find a way through until the game was into added time. Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner to level the scores before winning a penalty when he was dragged down by Victor Valdepenas in the box, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory. Later on Sunday, Atalanta host Frosinone and Genoa face Venezia before Juventus travel to Lecce and AC Milan go to Udinese. item.title: EPL: Carrick benches Bruno Fernandes after Como outburst
item.description: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said it was a “pure football” decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench despite the Portugal midfielder’s criticism of his manager’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como. Without a win in seven games in all competitions, Carrick badly needs a victory against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to quell speculation over his future and has made a bold call. The Red Devils begin the day 15th in the table with just seven points from their opening seven league games. Fernandes hit out at United’s passive approach out of possession as Champions League debutants Como ran riot in Italy on Wednesday. “When you have options it’s always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want,” added Carrick as he dismissed the decision was taken as a response to Fernandes’s outburst. Fernandes won a clean sweep of individual awards last season after breaking the Premier League record for assists with 21 as United finished third in the table. But the 32-year-old’s impact has been much more limited so far this season, bar a hat-trick against Ipswich back in August. Carrick made four changes in total with Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui also dropping out for Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo. Fernandes’s comments came just over a week after Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s board for not doing enough to strengthen Carrick’s squad in the transfer window. Martinez was not dropped for his remarks but was replaced at half-time in a 1-1 draw at Leeds last weekend with an injury and is only fit enough to return from the bench against Bournemouth. “You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players,” said United’s all-time leading goalscorer Wayne Rooney. He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. “If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.” Vanguard News The post EPL: Carrick benches Bruno Fernandes after Como outburst appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FRSC identifies persistent safety violations among tanker drivers
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has identified speeding, driver fatigue, overloading and driving against traffic as persistent violations among petroleum tanker drivers. The FRSC spokesman, Osondu Ohaeri who told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Abuja, warned that such practices continue to threaten road safety despite enforcement efforts. Ohaeri further discussed the challenges associated with the transportation of petroleum products and other goods by articulated vehicles. He said some tanker drivers exceeded recommended speed limits in attempts to meet delivery schedules, despite the difficulty of bringing heavily loaded vehicles to a safe stop. He explained that the size and weight of tankers required drivers to exercise caution, particularly when approaching bridges, bends and congested sections of highways. He also identified fatigue as a major risk, noting that some drivers attempted to cover long distances, including journeys from Kano to Lagos, overnight without adequate rest. “Driving while fatigued could impair concentration and reaction time, increasing the likelihood of losing control of vehicles. “Also, driving against traffic is another serious violation. Some operators overload their vehicles or use them to carry additional goods alongside petroleum products. “These practices can compromise vehicle stability and expose drivers, passengers and other road users to danger,” he said. Ohaeri attributed the persistence of the violations partly to drivers’ attitudes and the pressure to meet delivery schedules, stressing that compliance with traffic regulations remained essential regardless of operational demands. He said the FRSC had continued to intensify safety education and enforcement while working with operators and other stakeholders to improve compliance. He disclosed that the corps had achieved about 75 per cent success in issuing the appropriate Class G driver’s licences to relevant operators, as part of efforts to ensure that drivers possessed the required qualifications. He said the agency was also engaging petroleum marketers and other industry stakeholders to strengthen safety standards across the transportation chain. He urged tanker drivers and operators to prioritise safety over delivery schedules, warning that violations involving vehicles conveying highly flammable products could have devastating consequences. He called for improved driver discipline, adequate rest, proper vehicle maintenance and strict adherence to speed limits to reduce crashes involving articulated vehicles.
